links.reason: Verse 50's துறக்கம்-like claim (இந்திர உலகம் வந்து இழிந்த தொக்கும்) is a poet's simile for the city; 469 only has a Vidyadhara decide துறக்கம் மீது எனவே, and nothing in the Tamil says he stands in that same city. 'Outsider's verdict confirming the boast' rests on the marker's reading of the sarukkam title.
links.text_issue: 469 sense uncertain; whether the place is the city of 50 is not stated

links.reason: 2797 compares the body to a grove burned by the fire of disease (பிணி எனும் செந்தீ), 63 to a bubble on water (நீரில் குமிழி): different images, shared theme of impermanence. The verse asks nothing, so 'one asks escape from disease' is untrue; 'prayer for release' is only in the Siddhar.

496 asks ஈங்கெமக்கு நீர் பணிந்தது என்னை and 500 answers with அருந்தவம் செய்தார்களே, so question and answer are real. But 'those who bow at your feet have done penance' is a courtly compliment, so 'not mere flattery' is not shown by the Tamil.

107 has Amirthamathi list past-deed fruits (நின்று செய் பயன்); 217 has attendants say her state is karma's fruit (வினைப்பயனே). The law is the same, but in 217 it is the attendants' remark, not her argument turned on her, and 'her sickness' is not in the verse.

120 says worshippers of the lion-throne lord become தேவாதி தேவர் and reach முத்தி; Kural 10 says only those at இறைவன் அடி cross the sea. The verse names no 'sequence of worlds', and தேவாதிதேவருமாய் can be a rank of the released rather than a stage before release, so the graded-gain claim and both gains are overstated.

Akananuru 17 has the foster mother recall the girl tired from play lying in mother's arms (முயங்கினள் வதியும்) and now eloping; 1759 has a father seat his daughter and look over her body. The ball-play is not in 1759, the poem's arms are the mother's, and neither side genuinely gains from the other.

28 has brother, friends and wives all 'புலம் துறப்ப' while Civakan goes to விருந்து ஆர் கதி, which does cut against the question of Kural 46 (what is gained by going the outer way after a virtuous household). But 28 does not say he lived the household life justly, and the goal is left unnamed, so the conflict needs a generous reading.

Kural 64's சிறுகை அளாவிய கூழ் and Purananuru 188's சிறுகை நீட்டி, இட்டும் தொட்டும் கவ்வியும் துழந்தும் share the small child's hand in the food, and the shared 'அளாவு/துழ' act is the same. Kural makes the mess a sweetness beyond nectar, 188 makes its absence the verdict (பயக்குறை இல்லை தாம் வாழும் நாளே), which neither shows alone.

1862 has ministers say the sage's feet are the only refuge (அரண் பிறிது); 2003 has the sage say austerity is hard to tell. They are about 140 verses apart and 2003 never answers the ministers; 'taught in steps' is not in either Tamil text. The 'first reply' is a reconstruction.

Both verses set Murugan beside Civakan: 812 the kings cry மஞ்ஞையே முருகன் தான் in terror, 2548 the women call him முருகனம்பி and அநங்கன் with glad hearts (சிந்தையிற் களிப்பார்). The same likening carrying fear and desire in two audiences is accurate and specific, though modest.

1556 sets the white umbrella (வெண்குடை) over the world and then has the king caught in women's net (வலையிற் பட்டான்); Naladiyar 3's umbrella-riders fall by their deeds (வினை உலப்ப). Only the umbrella is shared, the net is love not the fall of deeds, and the quatrain gains nothing real from it.

1298's அருந்தவஞ் செய்து வந்த is the women's guess that rare penance earned the marriage; Kural 265 says penance is done because வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங்கு எய்தல். This illustrates the couplet's motive and is spoken by bewildered onlookers; 'heard as making penance the price of pleasure' is a reading, not a qualification.

1869's drum is heard by citizens who bless a long life (வாழ்க நம் இறைவன்) and Naladiyar 3's drum is மணப்பறை turned பிணப்பறை. No reversal or the king's resolve is in 1869; the irony the note supplies comes from outside the verse and the quatrain gains nothing from it.

1505's secrecy (அறிவுறா வகையின்) and Kural 1151's plea (செல்லாமை உண்டேல் எனக்குரை) do contrast, but Kemasari's words and loss are not in 1505, so 'given the words she never gets to say' is invented and the pairing is a thematic contrast rather than a qualification.

242 says Dattai fell into மயற்கை and 243 names the longing (விசும்பிற் செல்லும் வேட்கை). The second verse does answer the word of the first, but they are adjacent lines of one narration and 'sets the plot in motion' is plot, not a link.

Purananuru 90's tiger makes deer herds impossible (மறப்புலி உடலின் மான்கணம் உளவோ), Kural 599's tiger makes even a big tusked elephant fear (யானை அஞ்சும் புலிதாக்கு உறின்). Both are tiger-over-prey images, but the elephant is not a herd, and 'neither numbers nor size can resist' is a stretch of 599, whose words say nothing of energy.

594's ஆணையான் எரியும் and ஈகையான் குளிரும் name command and giving; Kural 390 lists கொடை, அளி, செங்கோல், குடியோம்பல். Giving matches, but ஆணை is not செங்கோல், and 'tempers not duties' and a missing 'picture' for the couplet are not in either Tamil.

1069's வெஞ்சொல் refers back to the word that 899 quotes (ஏற்பில என்ற சொல்), so the link to the contest is real. But 1069 nowhere mentions the vow or that the word 'earned' it, so 'names the double fruit' is the marker's reconstruction.

Kural 879 says cut the thorn tree while young (இளைதாக முள்மரம் கொல்க); 1894 says no foe is small (பகை சிறிதென்ன வேண்டா) and must be guarded against. The idea of a small harm growing deadly is shared, but 1894 gives no remedy opposed to striking early, so the contrast attack versus vigilance is a generous reading.

707 has Tivittan vow வாயைப் போழ்ந்து the lion, and 1135 reports இளைய காளை வாய்பிளந்திட்ட வார்த்தை so that the sky-dwellers tremble. The wording of the vow and its report matches, and the fulfilment is seen through the enemy's fear.

774's பெறு பயன் இல்லை for a body that cannot help the afflicted and Naladiyar 34's அரும்பெறல் யாக்கை, பெரும்பயன் கொள்க both treat the body's worth as its fruit. The quatrain adds that the body goes like cane refuse (கோதுபோல் போகும்), which 774 lacks, and 774 names the use (aid in trouble) that the quatrain leaves general.

888 has the maid say moist makes bad good and dry makes good bad (வாரம் பட்டுழித் தீயவும் நல்லவாம்), a point about the powders; Kural 504 tells a king to weigh குணம் and குற்றம். The claim that the maid strikes the 'method of judgement' and that the couplet assumes still qualities is read in, and neither verse speaks of a king choosing a man.

907 has the father make carved figures women (பாவை எல்லாம் கதிர்முலை ஆக்கினான்); 2003 has Civakan hide near the golden image of Kama. Nothing says Kama's image is male or left standing, and the two make no incompatible claims, so 'tension' and 'the gap' are invented.

2628 has the matrons board சிவிகை to their துறவு, and Tirumanthiram 153 has the lord mount a காட்டுச் சிவிகை, the bier. The shared vehicle and the turn from procession to renunciation is a pretty contrast, but 'taking the last ride first' is imported from outside the verse and the Tirumanthiram gains nothing it needs.

5's அறநன் மாரி is a figure for the lord's teaching; Kural 545's பெயல் is actual rain bound to the king's செங்கோல். The link matches the word 'rain' across a figure and a literal claim, and the verse does not say rain follows the king's justice.

Nedunalvadai 186-187 has the king sleepless at midnight walking (பள்ளி கொள்ளான் சிலரொடு திரிதரும்) to see wounds; Mullaippattu 67-76 has him sleepless (கண்படை பெறாது) thinking of wounded elephants and fallen men. The shared care is real, but one does not extend the other, so 'develops' is the wrong type.

1305 has Kamukan come with bow and arrow; Naladiyar 386 compares a modest woman's beauty to a sword in a hero's hand. The quatrain is about a woman's beauty, not about the hero, so the hero-and-weapon tie is a stretched simile; 'the next verse' is outside the packet.

3082 tells காதிப்போர் மன்னர் fall and omniscience; 3092 sings காதி நாலும் அரிந்து, மூன்று காலமும் உணர்ந்த கடவுள். The matter is repeated, but 3092 may praise the Lord generally, 'the narrator's story as hymn's ground' is not shown, and it is a hymn after the event.

232 has அறிவு எனும் அமைச்சன் speak to the king, and Kural 638 binds உழையிருந்தான் to speak. The topic of a minister's counsel is shared, but 232 does not give the counsel or say it comes too late, and the usurper's office is not in the verse.

Kural 1269 has one day like seven for those waiting; 2100 has பிரிந்த நாள் ஓர் ஊழி. The stretching of time by absence is the same, with a bigger measure. This is a parallel formula, not a qualification, and 'a man plainly speaking' adds nothing to the couplet.

1483 binds the breasts with கச்சு as கடியன கொடியன; Kural 1087 likens the cloth over her breasts to the elephant's கட்படாம். The epic has no elephant, and 'restraint on a dangerous force' is how the note reads both, so the shared image is only the covering.
759 makes wealth the sharpest எஃகு against enemy pride; 773 makes help to a fallen foe the எஃகு of valour. They share the word எஃகு, not a claim about one thing, so neither contradicts the other.

416 foretells குடையும் பிச்சமும் ஒழியக் கோன்படை உடையும், and 437 has the spear-army break leaving பிச்சம், and banners (பிச்சம் கொடியொடு இட்டு வேற்படை உடைந்த). The fulfilment is exact in the dropped standards; the trust claim goes a little further but is fair.

1603 says women climb the hill so that evil deeds leave (தீவினை நீங்க), a pilgrim's purpose reported by the narrator and not endorsed; Siddhar 696 says he walked every hill without seeing God within (கடமலை தோறுந் திரிந்து). Whether the narrator approves is not in the verse, and 'Jains and Saivas held in common' is not in either text.
1591 asks அடிமிசை ஈன்றது இவ் அசோகம் என்கொலோ, and 1592 answers அலத்தகச் சுவடு, women's lac footprints. The question is answered in the next verse by the king.

772 praises Tivittan for killing the lion that devoured the herds so that all sleep peacefully; Kural 550 compares the king's killing of the cruel to weeding. The weeding image and king's justice are not in 772, and 'a Jain poet has to justify' is the marker's, not the Tamil's.

462 has men cry in wonder at the Creator (என்ன பாவம்) for making these women; Tirumanthiram 204 warns off women like the etti fruit. But 204 itself blames the women's smile and breasts, so it does not put the remedy in 'a choice of the heart' against blaming another.

Kalavazhi 32 makes the Earth a woman wrapped red (செய்யது போர்த்தாள்போல்) with the victor's blood; 2221 has நிலமகள் beat her breast and pine. They do not contradict, so 'tension' is the wrong type; the shared figure with its change from dressed to mourner is better called a shared image. The 'counter-voice' gain for Kalavazhi is not in the Tamil.

1090 reports Sunandai and her husband calling going under the king's protection குணம்; 1093 has her fall into grief at the binding. Grief does not refute the counsel, so there is no tension, but the cost of the counsel is a fair reading.

945 has the hero whisper the five mantras into the dying creature's ear, and 3037 has a god praise his feet; the verse does not name the god or say he was the dog. The tie rests on the marker's reading of the next verse, and 'debt repaid' is not stated.
links.text_issue: 3037 subject taken from next verse; 945 line 4 hard to read

links.reason: 836 says the wedding was one that even Indra could not have (இந்திரன் தனக்கும் ஆகாது); Kural 1103 asks whether the lotus-eyed one's world is sweeter than sleep in a loved one's arms. Both rank a human union over a god's, but 836 speaks of the wedding done in a moment, not 'public splendour', so the contrast is not in the Tamil.

2220 counts Kattiyangaran's chariots, elephants, horses and foot; Kural 770 says without leaders there is no army. 2220 says nothing of leaders or of Civakan's force or the outcome, so the rule is not shown to apply.

Both are conditional self-curses: 71 'if I do not see their backs (புறம் காணேன் ஆயின்) may I be parted from this wife', 1043 'if I do not live with her may I be one who thought of striking the beaten'. The inversion is neat, but that the epic draws on the Sangam வஞ்சினக் காஞ்சி as its source is not shown by the Tamil, so the first gain overreaches.
